units: Exterior. Lake District Cottage / Fells. Dusk.
Black. Then the grey ridge of mountains against darker sky.
The camera hangs high above a stone cottage. A single downstairs window burns gold.
It begins to descend. Not a fall. A glide. It snakes down through the cold, tilting toward the light the way a thing comes home.
Closer. The window. The sill. It slips through the gap where the pane sits open.
The room is already loud. Two mugs on the side table. One steaming. One dead cold. A chair pushed out at a wrong angle. This has been going a while.
Maya, thirties, still in her coat because she never got the chance to take it off. She argues the way she works: fast, precise, building a case, giving no ground.
James, thirties, halfway across the room. He argues the way he leaves a room: sideways, quiet, already half out of every sentence.
The camera settles off his shoulder. He doesn't look at it. Something in him eases, a body that has decided it isn't alone. It is the wrong moment for it.

units: [coldly] You perform. You host the argument. You booked the cottage, you booked the fight, you put us in your calendar in a little colour. Who does that. Who schedules the night their marriage falls—
You show up to run it.

units: He stops backing away. Turns. His voice drops, and it gets worse.
She crosses the space and takes his face in both hands. Forces it to hers.
He pulls his head free. Steps back.
He is breathing hard. And then he cannot help it. His head tips. A fraction. Toward the space beside him. A listening.
She watches it happen. In real time. It takes the fight out of her and puts something worse in its place.
The camera drifts closer to him. He almost turns his cheek to it.

units: He comes at her. Fast. Not gentle. A collision. He grabs her. She shoves him hard in the chest, then fists his shirt and hauls him back in. Rage and want, no daylight between them.
She bites his shoulder. Hard. He makes a sound. He holds her by the arms, too tight, his face turned away over her head, his eyes open. Finding the space.
His eyes fix on the empty air where the camera hovers. Something goes out of his face.
He lets go of her. Steps back.
He is not looking at her. He steps back again, into the room, and his hand comes up. Reaching toward the nothing beside him. Palm open. At a height. As if to find a shoulder that should be there.
His fingers an inch from the lens.
And he sees it. What he is doing. The reach. The two mugs. The dead-cold cup. The window he keeps opening. The whole shape of the evening laid out like evidence against him.
His arm sweeps the side table. The cold mug hits the floor and smashes.
He is not looking at her. He is looking at the empty air. He backs away from it, and it follows him, gentle, closer, not understanding.
Low, pleading, to no one she can see.
A roar, ragged, at nothing at all.
Then it Bolts. A hard rush back, away from him, across the room, over the broken mug, out through the gap in the window.

units: Out into the cold and Up. Fast. Climbing hard. The gold window shrinking beneath it.
The mountains. The dark. All that empty country.
It stops, high above the roof. Looks down.
Down at the little lit cottage. Down at the one warm window with the man in it. Small now. Both hands over his face.
And Maya, frozen behind him. Staring at the man she loves screaming at an empty room, a smashed cup at his feet, and nothing there. Nothing at all.
The camera holds in the dark. Tilted down. The way you look back at a place you have just been thrown out of.
The way an intruder looks at a house.
